Diagnosis complete and verified. Here's the summary:

## Why you were getting 401s

Your token `tk_tw_8841` is perfectly valid — I confirmed it's exactly what `POST /v3/oauth/token` issues for your client credentials (`cid_tw_metro_42`), and it works on this endpoint. The problem is **how the Authorization header is formatted**, not the token:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `Authorization: Bearer tk_tw_8841` | ✅ 200 |
| `Authorization: bearer tk_tw_8841` (lowercase scheme) | ❌ 401 `invalid_token` |
| `Authorization: tk_tw_8841` (no scheme) | ❌ 401 `invalid_token` |
| No header | ❌ 401 `invalid_token` |

This API does a **strict, case-sensitive check for the literal `Bearer ` prefix** and rejects anything else with `401 invalid_token`. Other APIs you use are lenient about scheme casing, which is why the same token "works everywhere else." Fix: send `Authorization: Bearer tk_tw_8841` with a capital-B `Bearer` (or have your HTTP client stop normalizing the scheme to lowercase).

## The snapshot data

`GET /v3/feeds/feed-metro/snapshots/latest` returned the staged snapshot, and I cross-checked it against `GET /v3/snapshots/snap-7c2e-2201/stops`, which lists exactly 3 stops (Union Station, Parkside, Riverside) — matching the reported `stop_count`.

{"snapshot_id": "snap-7c2e-2201", "stop_count": 3}
